# Research Brief: UI/UX & Web-Conversion Design-Principles Taxonomy

**Generated by:** Claude (Gemini CLI brief route blocked by dispatch-route-guard; used the skill's sanctioned fallback — "Claude writes it directly")
**Date:** 2026-06-01
**Original query:** What is the canonical, evidence-based taxonomy of UI/UX & web-conversion design PRINCIPLES that a designer must master — the set that, if each were a teachable guide, would comprehensively cover product UI craft, visual/interaction design, accessibility, and landing-page conversion?

## Research Question

What is the canonical, evidence-based taxonomy of UI/UX and web-conversion design principles — a clustered set of ~12-18 self-contained, teachable topics — that comprehensively covers product UI craft, visual and interaction design, accessibility, and landing-page conversion, where each topic carries a stable slug, scope, depth tier, 3-5 authoritative grounding sources, and yields agent-checkable rules that collectively cover the design-quality gauntlet's six axes (design-tokens, component-usage, visual-hierarchy, mobile-responsive, accessibility, design-handoff) and visual-review's seven categories (color, layout, typography, copy, a11y, console-error, regression)?

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Landscape
Survey the canonical principle taxonomies that already exist and map overlaps: NN/g 10 heuristics, Laws of UX, Gestalt, Refactoring UI, WCAG 2.2 POUR, Material 3 / Apple HIG, Baymard/CXL conversion frameworks. Stop when 5+ taxonomies surveyed and overlap-mapped.

### Phase 2 — Mechanics
Determine the right granularity/clustering for a ~12-18 topic teachable taxonomy. Which principles get a standalone guide, which fold together, what cluster structure (Foundations / Visual / Interaction / Accessibility / Conversion / Systems) holds. Stop when a clustered taxonomy is justified against 3+ source structures.

### Phase 3 — Failure Modes
Identify the common, checkable failures each principle prevents, so each topic yields agent-applicable rules mirroring what visual-review and design-quality catch. Stop when each candidate topic has 2+ concrete checkable failure modes.

### Phase 4 — Contrarian
Challenge the taxonomy: where authorities disagree, what heuristic lists omit (motion, content design, performance UX, i18n, ethics/dark patterns). Stop when 2+ gaps/disagreements documented.

## Per-engine instructions

- **OpenAI o3-deep-research:** Construct a MECE ~12-18 topic taxonomy; per topic give UPPER_SNAKE slug, scope, cluster, 2-3 checkable rules; map full set to the 6 design-quality axes + 7 visual-review categories; flag any uncovered axis.
- **Gemini deep-research-pro:** Pull and compare canonical sources; extract recurring categories; produce a which-category-in-which-source comparison table.
- **Claude (3-round search):** Verify source authority/recency, reconcile overlapping categories into a deduplicated list, investigate the contrarian gaps.

## Coverage targets (must be satisfied by the final taxonomy)
- **design-quality axes:** design-tokens, component-usage, visual-hierarchy, mobile-responsive, accessibility, design-handoff
- **visual-review categories:** color, layout, typography, copy, a11y, console-error, regression
- **product-designer lenses:** cohort fit, cognitive load, state coverage, start-path fit, consistency, mobile/responsive
- **web-conversion-designer lenses:** above-the-fold, hierarchy (hook→proof→CTA), CTA prominence, friction/leaks, journey, mobile/responsive
